Title 3— 
The President 
Executive Order 13476 of October 9, 2008 
Facilitation of a Presidential Transition 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including section 7301 of title 5, 
United States Code, and the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention 
Act of 2004 (Public Law 108–458) (IRTPA), and in order to further the 
purposes of the Presidential Transition Act of 1963, as amended, and to 
assist the presidential transition, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Presidential Transition Coordination. (a) To assist and support 
the transition efforts of the transition teams for the ‘‘major party’’ ‘‘can-
didates,’’ as those terms are used in the IRTPA and defined in section 
9002(2) and (6) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (26 U.S.C. 9002(2), 
(6)), and the President-elect, there is established a Presidential Transition 
Coordinating Council (Council). 
(b) The Council shall be composed of the following officials or their 
designees: 
(i) Chief of Staff to the President, who shall serve as Chair; 
(ii) Assistant to the President and Deputy Chief of Staff for Operations, 
who shall serve as Vice Chair; 
(iii) Assistant to the President and Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy; 
(iv) Counsel to the President; 
(v) Assistant to the President for Presidential Personnel; 
(vi) Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs; 
(vii) Assistant to the President for Homeland Security and 
Counterterrorism; 
(viii) Assistant to the President for Economic Policy and Director, National 
Economic Council; 
(ix) Attorney General; 
(x) Director of National Intelligence; 
(xi) Director of the Office of Management and Budget; 
(xii) Director of the Office of Personnel Management; 
(xiii) Administrator of General Services; 
(xiv) Archivist of the United States; 
(xv) Director of the Office of Government Ethics; and 
(xvi) Such others as the President or the Chair of the Council may select. 
(c) The Council shall assist the major party candidates and the President- 
elect by making every reasonable effort to facilitate the transition between 
administrations. This assistance may include, among other things, providing 
information relevant to facilitating the personnel aspects of a presidential 
transition and such other information that, in the Council’s judgment, is 
useful and appropriate, as long as providing such information is not otherwise 
prohibited by law. 
(d) In order to obtain a wide range of facts and information on prior 
transitions and best practices, the Council, its members, or their designees

Sec. 2. Transition Activities and Materials. (a) At the direction of the Council

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13476 of October 9, 2008 (Facilitation of a Presidential Transition, 73 FR 60605, printed October 14, 2008) establishes a Presidential Transition Coordinating Council, directs transition activities and materials, and provides for transition agreements, all for the 2008 presidential transition. Section 4(d) fixes its own end: unless extended by the President, the order expires on February 20, 2009. The held registered text of the whole order was read; every operative clause is therefore time-limited by section 4(d), and the order's own terms end all of its clauses on that date. No extension is held: the bounded searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) and a search of the held order texts for the order's number found no later instrument that extends, amends or revokes it; the one catalog hit is the Federal Register note citing EO 13467 of June 30, 2008 (it also records that this order supersedes EO 13176), a cross-reference to the order that created the Suitability and Security Clearance Performance Accountability Council mentioned in section 2(c), not an ending or amendment of this order. Section 4(a) supersedes Executive Order 13176 of November 27, 2000; that supersession took effect on issue and is an accrued effect, not a continuing command. The whole-order end is February 20, 2009, recorded inclusive as the stated date (the exclusive reading, under which the order ended when that day began, is the alternative). Status recommended: no. The inventory is the machine segmentation of the order (31 scopes); it covers the text from section 1 through section 4(d), with section 1(a) split at an internal citation fragment and the lettered and numbered items of sections 1(b) and 4(b) listed as separate scopes, and no operative text is outside it.

savings_residuals.reason: The order states that it creates no right or benefit enforceable at law (section 4(c)) and confers no function independent of the Council it established. Transition agreements and Council activities were performed for the 2008-2009 transition; nothing in the held text or in the bounded searches shows any right, duty or program of this order continuing after its expiry on February 20, 2009. The Presidential Transition Act and the later transition orders are separate bases, not continuations of this order.
